# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, partly in the barony of Carey, chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Contains the post town of Bushmills and a portion of Dunserverick.
- **County seat:** Antrim town (county-level); Bushmills is the principal settlement in the civil parish.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Since 1922, County Antrim is part of Northern Ireland (UK). Records generated before 1922 are accessible from both the **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** and, for national record series, the **National Archives of Ireland (NAI)**.
- **Religious denominations confirmed in parish:** Church of Ireland (established church), Presbyterians, Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians), and Wesleyan Methodists. Catholic families are recorded under the **Coleraine RC district**, not a separate "Billy" Catholic parish.
- **Key historical note:** Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union that also comprised **Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride**. Registers from the union may be relevant for some families.

---

## Boundary & Administrative Changes

- Civil parish boundaries were fixed by the Ordnance Survey mapping (1830s) and were stable throughout 1780–1870.
- From 1922, the primary archive for county-level records shifted to PRONI in Belfast, while many pre-1922 national record series remain accessible from the NAI in Dublin.
- **Critical loss:** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers held centrally at the Public Record Office in Dublin were **destroyed in the 1922 fire** — the most significant documentary gap for Billy parish.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)

- Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths for **all denominations** began **1 January 1864** — covering only the final six years of the target period.
- Non-Catholic (Church of Ireland and Presbyterian) marriages have a slightly earlier registration start: **1845**.
- For **1780–1863**, church records are the *only* primary source for vital events.
- Civil registration records for County Antrim (Northern Ireland) are held by **GRONI** and accessible through PRONI.
- ⚠️ **IrishGenealogy.ie does NOT cover County Antrim.** Its free coverage is limited to County Kerry, parts of Cork, and Dublin City.

### Church Records

> **The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy Civil Parish contains empty section headings for all denominations** (Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends) — no specific register dates or microfilm numbers are entered. **Before searching, consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records** to identify which registers survive, their date ranges, and how to access them.

**Church of Ireland**
- Established church; records kept at the parochial level.
- Surviving originals for County Antrim are held by PRONI and the RCB Library in Dublin. PRONI holds microfilm copies of surviving registers.
- Because Billy was head of an ecclesiastical union (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride), search *all five* former union parishes for registers.
- [PRONI Guide to Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) — identifies which registers survive and their date ranges.
- [RCB Library list of surviving parish registers](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf)
- [PRONI Digitised Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1) — free online access to digitized registers.

**Catholic**
- Billy parish is in the **Catholic district of Coleraine** — search under *Coleraine* for Catholic records.
- Most rural Irish Catholic parishes did not begin registers until Catholic Emancipation (1828); coverage for 1780–1827 is likely sparse.
- [National Library of Ireland Digitised Catholic Registers](https://registers.nli.ie/) — **free**
- [Ancestry: Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/) — subscription
- Note: Catholic registers frequently lack burial registers; use cemetery records and Church of Ireland burial registers instead.

**Presbyterian (including Covenanting / Reformed Presbyterian)**
- Two distinct bodies were present: Synod of Ulster Presbyterians and Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians) — their registers are separate series.
- Presbyterian registers average a start date of 1830, though some go back to the 1600s.
- PRONI holds microfilm copies of Presbyterian registers for Northern Ireland.
- [Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland](https://www.presbyterianhistoryireland.com/) — College Park East, Belfast BT7 1LP — holds originals for some congregations and provides research guidance.
- [FindMyPast: Ireland Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) — subscription
- [FindMyPast: Ireland Non-Conformist Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) — subscription

**Methodist (Wesleyan)**
- Wesleyan Methodists had a meeting house in Billy parish; registers are generally held by PRONI.
- [FindMyPast: Ireland Non-Conformist Congregational Records](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) — subscription

---

### Census Substitutes (1780–1870)

No original Irish census records survive for this period (1861/1871 censuses destroyed in WWI; 1841/1851 largely destroyed in the 1922 fire). Use:

| Record | Dates | Coverage | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | All principal landholders in Billy's townlands | FamilySearch (catalog search); Ancestry |
| Flaxseed Premium Lists | 1796 | County Antrim farmers who received spinning wheels/looms — a 1796 name list | FamilySearch |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | 1847–1864 | Every occupier of land or buildings — the most comprehensive name list for the 1850s–60s | [AskAboutIreland.ie](http://www.askaboutireland.ie/) (free index); Ancestry; FindMyPast; PRONI |
| 1901 & 1911 Census | Post-period | Full survival; use to anchor families and project back | [NAI Census](https://census.nationalarchives.ie/) — free |

---

### Probate & Wills

- **Prerogative Court of Armagh (before 1858):** Original wills destroyed in the 1922 fire. Key substitutes:
  - [FindMyPast: Betham Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) — subscription
  - [FindMyPast: Crossle Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/crossle-genealogical-abstracts) — subscription
  - [FindMyPast: Thrift Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) — subscription
  - [Ancestry: Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/) — subscription
- **District probate registries (from 1858):** PRONI holds surviving testamentary records for Northern Ireland from 1858 onward.

---

### Marriage License Bonds — Key Substitute for Destroyed Registers

For Church of Ireland families, marriage license bonds are a critical substitute for destroyed registers. Billy parish falls within the **Diocese of Connor**.

- [FamilySearch: Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) — **free**
- [FindMyPast: Ireland Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage Licence Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-diocesan-and-prerogative-marriage-licence-bonds-indexes-1623-1866) — subscription

---

### Land Records

- **Registry of Deeds (from 1708):** Deeds, mortgages, marriage settlements voluntarily registered. PRONI holds microfilm. [Registry of Deeds](https://www.prai.ie/registry-of-deeds/) — Henrietta Street, Dublin D01 YH52.
- **Estate papers at PRONI:** Many north Antrim townlands were held by large landed estates. Estate papers can name tenants never found in standard registry records. Search PRONI's online catalogue: [https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni)
- **Valuation Revision Books (from 1864):** Track property changes year by year after Griffith's Valuation. Held at PRONI and the Valuation Office, Dublin.
- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s):** Survive in transcript for much of County Antrim; held at PRONI.

---

### Military Records

- [The National Archives (UK), Kew](https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/) — British Army service records, pension records, description books — TW9 4DU, Richmond, Surrey.
- **1798 Rebellion:** Rebellion Papers and State of the Country Papers at NAI Dublin; related depositions at PRONI.
- **Antrim Militia and local units:** PRONI holds muster rolls and militia records.

---

### Cemetery Records

- [Ulster Historical Foundation / RootsIreland](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) — indexed transcriptions of County Antrim gravestone inscriptions and church records; fee per search.
- [FindAGrave](https://www.findagrave.com/) and [BillionGraves](https://billiongraves.com/) — some Ulster transcriptions (coverage of Billy-area cemeteries unverified).
- Note: Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently lack burial records. Headstone inscriptions and Church of Ireland burial registers are the main burial sources for 1780–1870.

---

### Newspapers

- **Coleraine Chronicle** — local paper covering north Antrim; obituaries, marriage announcements, legal notices from the mid-19th century.
- **Belfast News-Letter** — covers Ulster from the 18th century.
- [British Newspaper Archive / FindMyPast](https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) — main digitized source for UK and Irish provincial papers; subscription.
- [Irish Newspaper Archives](https://www.irishnewsarchive.com/)
- [Linen Hall Library, Belfast](https://www.linenhall.com/) — 17 Donegall Square North, Belfast BT1 5GB — Northern Ireland historical newspapers and local history collections.

---

## Repository Summary

### Online Repositories

| Repository | Key Collections | Access | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Marriage License Bonds 1623–1866; Catholic Qualification & Convert Rolls 1701–1845; microfilmed registers (Catalog) | Free | https://www.familysearch.org |
| National Library of Ireland | Digitized Catholic parish registers | Free | https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| PRONI Digitised Church Records | Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist registers | Free | https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni |
| AskAboutIreland | Griffith's Valuation index | Free | http://www.askaboutireland.ie/ |
| NAI Census | 1901 and 1911 census images | Free | https://census.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| Ancestry | Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915; civil registration indexes; Griffith's; Tithe Books; wills abstracts | Subscription | https://www.ancestry.com |
| FindMyPast | Non-Conformist births/marriages/burials/congregational records; wills abstracts; British Newspaper Archive | Subscription | https://www.findmypast.com |
| RootsIreland / Ulster Historical Foundation | County Antrim indexed church and cemetery transcriptions | Fee per search | http://www.rootsireland.ie/ |

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Address |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** | Church register microfilm; estate papers; civil registration from 1864; Griffith's; wills from 1858; militia records | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ — proni@communities-ni.gov.uk — https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| **GRONI** | Civil registration (births/marriages/deaths from 1864) for Northern Ireland | Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL — https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/groni |
| **RCB Library (Church of Ireland)** | Surviving Church of Ireland parish registers; list of all surviving registers | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 D14 N735 — library@ireland.anglican.org — https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| **Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland** | Original registers for some Presbyterian congregations | College Park East, Belfast BT7 1LP — https://www.presbyterianhistoryireland.com/ |
| **National Archives of Ireland (NAI)** | Pre-partition national records; Rebellion Papers; Registry of Deeds microfilm | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 — mail@nationalarchives.ie — https://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| **Registry of Deeds, Dublin** | Deeds, mortgages, and marriage settlements from 1708 | Henrietta Street, Dublin D01 YH52 — https://www.prai.ie/registry-of-deeds/ |
| **The National Archives (UK)** | British Army service and pension records | Kew, Richmond, Surrey TW9 4DU — https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ |
| **Linen Hall Library** | Northern Ireland historical newspapers; local history | 17 Donegall Square North, Belfast BT1 5GB — https://www.linenhall.com/ |

---

## Known Record Losses

1. **Church of Ireland parish registers (1922 PRO fire):** Two-thirds of registers held in Dublin were destroyed. Whether Billy's specific registers survived is not confirmed here — check the RCB Library's register list and PRONI.
2. **Prerogative Court wills (pre-1858):** Destroyed in 1922. Use Betham, Crossle, and Thrift abstract collections.
3. **Census records 1841, 1851, 1861, 1871:** No Irish census records survive for the 1780–1870 period. Use Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation as substitutes.

---

## Research Tips

- **Start at PRONI.** Consult the [PRONI Guide to Church Records](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) to find out which congregation registers survive, their date ranges, and whether they are on microfilm or digitized.
- **Know the denomination.** Catholic records are under *Coleraine* RC district. Presbyterian and Covenanter registers are separate series. Identification determines which record set to pursue first.
- **Search all five former union parishes** (Billy, Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) for Church of Ireland registers — records may have been kept at the union level.
- **Search Church of Ireland records even for non-CoI families.** These registers are often earlier and more complete, and sometimes recorded events for neighboring denominations informally.
- **Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently lack burial records.** For burials 1780–1870, rely on Church of Ireland burial registers and headstone inscriptions (RootsIreland / Ulster Historical Foundation).
- **IrishGenealogy.ie does not cover County Antrim** — do not rely on it.
- **The 1901 and 1911 censuses are your anchor.** Identify residents in Billy's townlands, then work backward through Griffith's Valuation, the Tithe Applotment Books, and church registers.
- **Search the FamilySearch Catalog directly** (https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog) for "Billy," "Bushmills," and "Antrim" to identify all microfilmed holdings for this area.

- **FindMyPast Non-Conformist Congregational Records** (index, subscription): http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records

**Other Nonconformist / Society of Friends**
- The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy lists a Society of Friends section, which is also empty. Given the geography (north Antrim coast), Quaker presence was not prominent, but the option exists to check. PRONI holds Irish Quaker records for Northern Ireland.

### Census records

- **1780-1870 target period:** No Irish census records survive for this period. The censuses of 1861 and 1871 were destroyed by government order during World War I. The 1841 and 1851 census records were largely destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire (some fragments survive).
- **Pre-census substitutes (within target period):**
  - **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-37):** A survey of landholders liable for tithes; covers the townlands of Billy parish. Available at FamilySearch (search the catalog) and on Ancestry.
  - **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847-64):** A comprehensive valuation of all landholders in Ireland; the most important substitute census source for the 1780-1870 period. The Billy parish portion falls within this date range. Index freely searchable at AskAboutIreland.ie; full images on Ancestry and FindMyPast. Also available at PRONI.
- **Post-period note:** The 1901 and 1911 Irish censuses survive completely and are freely available at the National Archives of Ireland (https://census.nationalarchives.ie/) and on Ancestry. While these fall after the target period, they are highly useful for reverse-projecting families back into 1780-1870.

### Probate and court records

- **Prerogative Court of Armagh (before 1858):** This court had jurisdiction over wills of significant value for all of Ireland. Its original records were destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire. Abstracts survive in several collections:
  - **Betham Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast, subscription): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts — abstracts of wills and other records collected by Sir William Betham; a key substitute for the 1922 losses.
  - **Crossle Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast, subscription): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/crossle-genealogical-abstracts
  - **Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast, subscription): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts
  - **Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591-1866** (Ancestry, subscription): https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/
- **District probate registries (from 1858):** When civil probate was reorganized in 1858, district registries were established. County Antrim wills would generally go to the Armagh or Londonderry district registry. PRONI holds surviving testamentary records for Northern Ireland from 1858 onward.
- **Marriage license bonds (substitute for missing registers):** For Church of Ireland families, marriage license bonds are an important substitute for destroyed registers. FamilySearch holds Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866 (index + images, free): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239. Also on FindMyPast (subscription): http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-diocesan-and-prerogative-marriage-licence-bonds-indexes-1623-1866. Billy parish falls within the Diocese of Connor, so Connor diocese bonds are the relevant series.

### Land records

- **Registry of Deeds (from 1708):** The Registry of Deeds in Dublin holds transcripts of deeds, mortgages, and marriage settlements that were voluntarily registered. PRONI holds microfilm copies.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-37):** See Census substitutes above.
- **Griffith's Valuation (1847-64):** See Census substitutes above.
- **Estate papers:** Many north Antrim townlands were held by large landed estates (including the Antrim estates and the Dunluce area). PRONI holds estate papers that can name tenants, including those who never appear in standard registry records. Search PRONI's online catalogue (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni) for Billy or the relevant townland names.
- **Land distribution jurisdiction:** Under the Penal Laws era (1780s), the Registry of Deeds in Dublin was the principal instrument for recording property interests. County-level records are at PRONI.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts (1780-1870):** The 1798 Rebellion (United Irishmen uprising, with significant action in Ulster), Napoleonic Wars service (1803-1815), and Crimean War (1853-56).
- **British Army service records:** The National Archives (TNA), Kew, Richmond, Surrey, TW9 4DU (https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/) holds service records, pension records, and description books for British Army soldiers.
- **1798 Rebellion records:** The Rebellion Papers and related State of the Country Papers are at the NAI, Dublin. PRONI holds related depositions and papers.
- **Pension records:** PRONI holds Royal Hospital Kilmainham pension records for Irish soldiers.
- **Muster rolls and militia records:** PRONI holds records of the Antrim Militia and other locally raised units.

### Cemetery records

- **Where held:** Sexton records for the major Bushmills-area cemeteries (Billy Church of Ireland graveyard, Presbyterian burial grounds) are held locally or at PRONI.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) and BillionGraves (https://billiongraves.com/) contain some Ulster transcriptions but coverage of Billy-area cemeteries is unverified from tool results.
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** has published graveyard surveys for County Antrim: http://www.ancestryireland.com/
- Note: Catholic and Presbyterian church registers in Ireland frequently do not contain burial registers (Ireland Church Records wiki page). Cemetery headstone inscriptions and Church of Ireland burial registers are the main burial record sources for the period.

### Newspaper records

- **Coleraine Chronicle:** A local paper covering north Antrim and Coleraine. Coverage of the area from the mid-19th century onward. Obituaries, marriage announcements, legal notices.
- **Belfast News-Letter:** One of the oldest newspapers in the British Isles; covers Ulster from the 18th century.
- **Where held:** The British Newspaper Archive on FindMyPast (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/, subscription) is the main digitized source for UK and Irish provincial papers. PRONI and local libraries hold microfilm of county-level papers.
- The Linen Hall Library, Belfast, and the Irish Newspaper Archives (https://www.irishnewsarchive.com/) also hold significant newspaper holdings.

### Immigration and emigration records

- North Antrim was a major source of 18th-19th century Ulster-Scots emigration to North America, particularly in waves during and after the 1780s, the 1798 Rebellion, the early 19th-century economic depression, and the Famine (1845-52).
- **Passenger lists:** For emigration to North America, passenger lists arriving at US ports are held at the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) and are searchable through Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- **Naturalization records:** Declarations of intention (first papers) and petitions for naturalization were filed at federal, state, and local courts and can be searched at Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- **PRONI emigration records:** PRONI holds some landlord-assisted emigration records and correspondence that may name Billy-area emigrants. Search the PRONI online catalogue.
- **Ireland, Emigration and Immigration** FamilySearch wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Emigration_and_Immigration

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-37):** Covered in Census substitutes above. Name principal householders; functionally the best pre-census name list for Billy parish.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847-64):** Covered above. Lists every occupier of land or buildings; effectively a comprehensive name list for the Billy area in the 1850s-60s.
- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s):** An earlier tax record that survives in transcript for much of County Antrim. Available at PRONI.
- **Flaxseed Premium Lists (1796):** Lists of County Antrim farmers who received spinning wheels or looms as incentives; functionally a census substitute for 1796. Available on FamilySearch.

### Other record types

- **Valuation Revision Books (from 1864):** After Griffith's Valuation, the revisions ("cancelled books") tracked property changes year by year. Held at PRONI and the Valuation Office, Dublin. Useful for tracking family property from the 1860s onward.
- **Schools records:** National Schools were established from 1831. School registers and inspection books for Billy-area schools may survive at PRONI.
- **Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds, 1623-1866** at FamilySearch (Connor diocese): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 — particularly important as a substitute for Church of Ireland registers lost in 1922.
- **Ireland, Catholic Qualification and Convert Rolls, 1701-1845:** FamilySearch, index + images (free): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3499248 — records of Catholics who swore oaths of allegiance or converted, by name.

## Records NOT online

- **Church registers for Billy parish's specific congregations:** The PRONI Guide to Church Records is the only confirmed way to identify which registers survive and which have been digitized. Many pre-1870 registers for north Antrim congregations are on microfilm at PRONI but not freely available online.
- **Estate papers:** Manuscript estate records that name tenants are at PRONI but are not indexed online by person name.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (originals):** Held at NAI; microfilm copies at PRONI. Some images available on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- **Valuation Revision Books:** At PRONI; not comprehensively indexed online.
- **Militia and local military records:** At PRONI; largely not online.
- **Registry of Deeds records:** Microfilm at PRONI and NAI; indexed by grantor/grantee but not freely full-text searchable.
- **Hearth Money Rolls transcripts:** At PRONI; some published but not fully online.

## Known record losses

- **Church of Ireland parish registers:** The Ireland Church Records FamilySearch wiki page states that two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers held at the Public Record Office in Dublin were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Whether Billy's specific Church of Ireland registers were among the destroyed or surviving one-third is not stated in any tool result returned during this survey; consult the RCB Library's list of surviving registers (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) and PRONI to determine survival.
- **Prerogative Court wills (pre-1858):** The 1922 PRO fire destroyed original wills from the Prerogative Court. Betham, Crossle, and Thrift abstract collections at FindMyPast are the principal surviving substitutes (source: Ireland Church Records wiki page).
- **Census records 1861 and 1871:** Destroyed (not mentioned explicitly in the tool results for this survey, but is a known record loss for all Irish research). No census records survive for the period 1780-1870; use Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation as substitutes.

## Research tips

- **The FamilySearch Wiki church records section for Billy is empty.** The Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) contains section headings for Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends, and Others but no specific register dates or microfilm numbers. Before searching any register, consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) to identify what registers exist for Billy's specific congregations, their start dates, and how to access them.
- **Identify the denomination before searching church records.** The Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) notes that Protestants and Catholics tended to live in clustered communities. Knowing the family's denomination will determine which register series to prioritize. Catholic records for Billy are filed under the Coleraine RC district, not under Billy.
- **Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union** comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. For Church of Ireland records, the ecclesiastical parish boundaries may not match the civil parish. Registers may have been kept at the union level or may have survived only for one of the former union parishes. Search all five former union parishes' records.
- **Search available Church of Ireland records even if the family was not Church of Ireland**, as the Ireland Church Records wiki page advises. Church of Ireland registers are often earlier and more complete than Catholic or Dissenter registers, and they sometimes recorded events for neighboring denominations informally.
- **Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently lack burial registers** (Ireland Church Records wiki page). For burials in the 1780-1870 period, rely on Church of Ireland burial registers (if not destroyed in 1922) and headstone inscriptions. The Ulster Historical Foundation (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) has published graveyard surveys for County Antrim.
- **For the entire period 1780-1863, church records are the only primary vital record source.** Civil registration did not begin until 1864. Non-Catholic marriages have a slightly earlier registration start (1845), but even those are not online for County Antrim via the same free portals as the Republic of Ireland.
- **IrishGenealogy.ie does NOT cover County Antrim.** The Ireland Church Records wiki page confirms that IrishGenealogy.ie's coverage is limited to County Kerry, western/northwestern County Cork, and most of Dublin City. Do not rely on it for Billy parish research.
- **The 1901 and 1911 censuses are an anchor point.** Use them to identify residents of Billy's townlands, then work backward to church registers, Griffith's Valuation (1847-64), and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823-37).
- **FamilySearch Wiki place-page tool outage:** All four wiki_place_page sections (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips) returned only a generic page with no Ireland-specific content during this survey. These pages may well exist on the FamilySearch Wiki. Re-run this locality guide before relying on their absence, and check https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Genealogy and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/County_Antrim,_Ireland_Genealogy directly.

---

Billy civil parish is a small north Antrim coastal parish centered on Bushmills that for the entire period 1780-1863 has no civil vital records — only church registers, land surveys, and wills stand between a researcher and a complete documentary gap. For 1864-1870, civil registration just begins and the records are at PRONI in Belfast. The most important first step for anyone researching this parish is to consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records, which will identify which specific congregation registers survive, what years they cover, and whether they are on microfilm or digitized. For Catholic families, the National Library of Ireland's free digitized registers at registers.nli.ie and Ancestry's Catholic Parish Registers collection cover the Coleraine RC district that includes Billy. For Presbyterian and other Dissenter families, PRONI microfilm, the Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland, and FindMyPast's non-conformist collections are the main online paths.

The next step is to consult PRONI's Guide to Church Records and to search the FamilySearch Catalog directly for Billy and Antrim-area registers, then build a research plan around whichever specific register series cover the family's denomination and townland.

### Federal Census Records ⭐ *Best starting point*
- **FamilySearch volume** (imageGroup 007621224): Covers 1850–1860, 412 images, **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable** — the most accessible digitized record for this period
- **Ancestry:** "1850 United States Federal Census - Schuylkill County" at `https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/` (subscription required)

- **FamilySearch volume** (imageGroup 004288771): Lutheran church records, **1840–1875**, 198 images
  - ⚠️ **Browse-only** — 0% name-indexed, NOT full-text searchable; must be paged through image by image

- Note: Schuylkill County's large immigrant mining population means Catholic and Lutheran church records are often the *only* documentation of births, marriages, and deaths — check denominational archives beyond what FamilySearch has digitized

### Probate & Court Records
- **FamilySearch collection** "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" (collection ID: 1999196): 3.2 million images, 0 indexed — images exist but are not name-searchable

  - Only **4% name-indexed**, but **full-text searchable** — use full-text search first, then browse

### Vital Records (Births, Marriages, Deaths)
- **No civil registration collection** for this period was found online
- Pennsylvania did not have statewide civil registration in the 1840s–1860s
- **Alternatives:** Church records and probate records are the primary substitutes

- No 1840s–1860s tax records were found online — consult the county courthouse or Pennsylvania State Archives

- Vital records (no civil registration for this period)

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840-1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky, United States
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by the survey tools. Pulaski County is in south-central Kentucky.
- **Economy:** Agriculture (subsistence farming, tobacco) dominant; modest commercial activity at Somerset
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly native-born Americans of Scots-Irish and English descent, with small German and other immigrant communities
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest denominations in Kentucky per the [Kentucky Church Records wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records); local congregations of these denominations operated in Pulaski County during the period
- **Key historical events:** The Civil War (1861-1865) significantly disrupted county administration; Kentucky's border-state status meant divided loyalties and both Union and Confederate military activity

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County boundaries were stable throughout 1840-1880; no subdivisions or annexations are noted in the tool results
- Records before county formation (1799) were held under Lincoln and Green counties; search those counties for ancestors documented before Pulaski County's organization

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** County-level birth and death registration: 1853-1862, 1874-1878, and 1892-1910 — all with minimal compliance. Statewide registration began in 1911 with general compliance by 1917. Marriage bonds are county-level from county formation (1799). Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **What exists:** Marriage bonds and licenses from 1799 (county level). Birth and death records from the partial registration periods 1853-1862 and 1874-1878 — but compliance was poor and many events were not registered
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (100 N. Main Street, #208, Somerset, KY 42502) for marriage bonds and licenses. Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort, holds microfilmed pre-1911 county records. FamilySearch has marriage bonds and consent forms from 1799-1871 digitized ([Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy))
- **Gaps:** No births or deaths were required to be registered for most of the 1840-1880 window. The 1871 courthouse disaster likely destroyed some records from that era
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers (Baptist, Methodist, Catholic, Presbyterian), family bibles, cemetery records, and mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880)

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest in Kentucky. Local congregations in Pulaski County served the period
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials, membership rolls, and church minutes
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collections include: *Kentucky Church Records, 1818-1995* (index and images, incomplete); *Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839-1960* (index only); *Kentucky Marriages, 1785-1979* (index only); *Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843-1970* (index only). Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records). The Pulaski County Historical Society holds the most comprehensive collection of local church records and obituaries. Denominational archives: Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), various Methodist conference archives, Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia)
- **Language:** English

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 all cover the target period. Kentucky federal census records begin in 1810 per [Kentucky, United States Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy)
- **State census:** Kentucky did not take state censuses
- **Other enumerations:** Federal mortality schedules for 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 record deaths in the year preceding each census — a valuable substitute for missing death records
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed and imaged on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription). FamilySearch `collections_search` and `volume_search` tools returned 0 results for this place during the survey — likely a place-resolution gap in the tools, not absence of records. Search FamilySearch directly at familysearch.org

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, guardianships, estate inventories, court orders, civil and criminal cases
- **Date range:** Pulaski County probate records begin 1801; court records begin 1799. Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse. FamilySearch has early will books (1801-1929) digitized. KDLA holds microfilmed copies. A disaster in 1871 destroyed some records — expect gaps
- **Note:** For a person who died testate (with a will), search will books; for intestate estates, search administration files

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state, not a rectangular-survey state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) holds original grants, warrants, surveys, and patents. Virginia granted lands in Kentucky before 1792. Per [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property): Old Kentucky Grants (1793-1856) and Kentucky Land Warrants (1816-1873) cover most of the target period
- **Types:** Deeds (person-to-person transfers), land grants and patents, warrants, surveys; deeds may name a wife by given name, a prior residence, or names of heirs
- **Date range:** County deed books from 1799; land grants from 1793 at the state level
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse holds deed books. Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) holds grants and patents. FamilySearch has *Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records, 1700-1955* — digitized images. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846-1848); Civil War (1861-1865) — the most significant; men on both Union and Confederate sides
- **Record types:** Service records and pension files at NARA; bounty land warrants (pre-1856); state adjutant general records at KDLA
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington DC and regional facilities) for federal records. KDLA (Frankfort) for state-level Kentucky military records. Fold3 (fold3.com, subscription) indexes many Civil War service and pension records

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Numerous rural family cemeteries and church cemeteries throughout Pulaski County; specific names were not listed in returned tool results
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (findagrave.com) covers many Kentucky cemeteries; BillionGraves is an additional resource
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual congregations and the Pulaski County Historical Society

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Specific paper names and dates for Pulaski County were not returned by the survey tools; Somerset was the county seat and likely had a local paper by the 1850s-1860s
- **Where held:** Newspapers.com (subscription) and the Kentucky Digital Library (kdl.kyvl.org) index Kentucky newspapers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate notices, and legal advertisements supplement sparse vital records

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Pulaski County is inland; any immigrant ancestors likely arrived through East Coast ports (Baltimore, New York, Philadelphia, New Orleans). The Cumberland Gap corridor brought many early settlers overland
- **Record types:** Passenger lists at NARA; naturalization records at the Pulaski County Circuit Court (pre-1906, naturalizations could be filed in any court of record); alien registrations (post-period)
- **Where held:** NARA for passenger lists. Pulaski County Courthouse for local naturalizations. FamilySearch and Ancestry index pre-1906 naturalizations
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property tax lists and personal property tax lists
- **Date range:** From county formation (1799)
- **Where held:** KDLA holds microfilmed Kentucky county tax lists. Some are on FamilySearch and Ancestry
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are available for every year (not just census years) and can document a person's presence in the county between censuses or substitute for missing census years

### Other record types
- **County court minute books:** Record county business beyond litigation — road assignments, poor relief, payments to local officials, and other matters naming residents
- **Pulaski County Historical Society vertical files:** The society maintains surname files and the most comprehensive local church record and obituary collection per the FamilySearch Wiki
- **Town and county histories:** 19th- and early 20th-century county histories often transcribe early records and may be the only surviving copy of records since lost

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Will books 1801-1929 (digitized); marriage bonds 1799-1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818-1995; Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839-1960; Kentucky Marriages 1785-1979; Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843-1970; Kentucky Land Office records 1700-1955 | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | Federal census, county tax lists, vital records indexes, land grants | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Civil War service records, pension files | Subscription |
| Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal census images, military records, passenger lists | Free/fee |

**Coverage of this survey:** The `collections_search` tool returned 0 results at both the county and Kentucky state level; `volume_search` similarly returned 0 results at both levels; `catalog_search` returned 0 hits at both levels. All three tools returned an empty resolved place (`standardPlace: ""`), indicating a place-resolution gap in the tools during this session — not confirmed absence of records. The FamilySearch Wiki for Pulaski County specifically names digitized collections available on FamilySearch. Researchers should search FamilySearch and Ancestry directly rather than relying on these tool-returned counts.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main St. #208, Somerset, KY 42502 | Marriage bonds and licenses from 1799; deed books from 1799; court order books from 1799; wills and probate from 1801 | In-person or mail request |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records; state military records | In-person; some records online via kdla.ky.gov |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscripts, newspapers, genealogical collections, land records | In-person; some digital resources |
| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset | Surname vertical files; church records; local newspaper obituaries | In-person; contact society for hours |
| University of Kentucky Special Collections, Lexington | Manuscripts, county histories, regional collections | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- Full county deed books (beyond the land grant/patent collections) — courthouse or KDLA microfilm
- Court order books and civil/criminal case files — courthouse or KDLA microfilm
- Pre-1911 county birth and death registers from the partial registration periods (1853-1862 and 1874-1878) — KDLA microfilm; compliance was poor and many registers are incomplete
- Local church registers not captured in FamilySearch's incomplete Kentucky Church Records collection — individual congregations or Pulaski County Historical Society
- County tax lists for most years — KDLA microfilm (some on FamilySearch and Ancestry)
- Sexton and burial records from private cemeteries

## Known record losses
The [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) states that a disaster destroyed some county records in 1838 and again in 1871. The 1871 loss falls within the target period and may affect court, deed, and probate records created before that date. No tool result specified which record series were lost or survived. Researchers should contact the Pulaski County Courthouse and KDLA to determine which specific volumes survived.

## Research tips
- Vital events in 1840-1880 are largely undocumented in civil records due to poor compliance with county registration laws (active only 1853-1862 and 1874-1878 per [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)). Prioritize church registers, mortality schedules, and cemetery records for births and deaths
- Marriage bonds are the most complete vital-event record series for the period — they are county-level from 1799 and are digitized on FamilySearch through 1871 per [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- Kentucky land records are state-land (not federal-land): look to the Kentucky Land Office in Frankfort for grants and patents, not the BLM General Land Office. Deed books at the county courthouse record person-to-person transfers and often name wives by given name, prior residences, and heirs. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- The Pulaski County Historical Society maintains surname vertical files and holds the most comprehensive local church record and obituary collection — contact them early in research
- Tax lists exist for every year and can document presence in the county when census records are missing or when a person is between federal enumerations
- Civil War service affected virtually every family; Kentucky men served on both Union and Confederate sides. Search both sets of records at NARA and on Fold3
- The 1871 records disaster means some courthouse records from before that date are lost — when a deed or court record is missing, check whether a contemporary copy or abstract survives in the KDLA microfilm or in county history publications
- Neighboring counties were not listed in the returned tool results (the Pulaski County Genealogy page did not include a Neighboring Counties table). Identify and check all bordering counties — families near county lines frequently generated records on both sides

# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840-1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky, United States
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by the survey tools. Pulaski County is in south-central Kentucky.
- **Economy:** Agriculture (subsistence farming, tobacco) dominant; modest commercial activity at Somerset
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly native-born Americans of Scots-Irish and English descent, with small German and other immigrant communities
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest denominations in Kentucky per the [Kentucky Church Records wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records); local congregations of these denominations operated in Pulaski County during the period
- **Key historical events:** The Civil War (1861-1865) significantly disrupted county administration; Kentucky's border-state status meant divided loyalties and both Union and Confederate military activity

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County boundaries were stable throughout 1840-1880; no subdivisions or annexations are noted in the tool results
- Records before county formation (1799) were held under Lincoln and Green counties; search those counties for ancestors documented before Pulaski County's organization

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** County-level birth and death registration: 1853-1862, 1874-1878, and 1892-1910 — all with minimal compliance. Statewide registration began in 1911 with general compliance by 1917. Marriage bonds are county-level from county formation (1799). Source: [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **What exists:** Marriage bonds and licenses from 1799 (county level). Birth and death records from the partial registration periods 1853-1862 and 1874-1878 — but compliance was poor and many events were not registered
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (100 N. Main Street, #208, Somerset, KY 42502) for marriage bonds and licenses. Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort, holds microfilmed pre-1911 county records. FamilySearch has marriage bonds and consent forms from 1799-1871 digitized ([Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy))
- **Gaps:** No births or deaths were required to be registered for most of the 1840-1880 window. The 1871 courthouse disaster likely destroyed some records from that era
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers (Baptist, Methodist, Catholic, Presbyterian), family bibles, cemetery records, and mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880)

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest in Kentucky. Local congregations in Pulaski County served the period
- **Record types:** Baptisms/christenings, marriages, burials, membership rolls, and church minutes
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collections include: *Kentucky Church Records, 1818-1995* (index and images, incomplete); *Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839-1960* (index only); *Kentucky Marriages, 1785-1979* (index only); *Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843-1970* (index only). Source: [Kentucky Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records). The Pulaski County Historical Society holds the most comprehensive collection of local church records and obituaries. Denominational archives: Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), various Methodist conference archives, Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia)
- **Language:** English

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 all cover the target period. Kentucky federal census records begin in 1810 per [Kentucky, United States Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy)
- **State census:** Kentucky did not take state censuses
- **Other enumerations:** Federal mortality schedules for 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 record deaths in the year preceding each census — a valuable substitute for missing death records
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed and imaged on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription). FamilySearch `collections_search` and `volume_search` tools returned 0 results for this place during the survey — likely a place-resolution gap in the tools, not absence of records. Search FamilySearch directly at familysearch.org

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, guardianships, estate inventories, court orders, civil and criminal cases
- **Date range:** Pulaski County probate records begin 1801; court records begin 1799. Source: [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse. FamilySearch has early will books (1801-1929) digitized. KDLA holds microfilmed copies. A disaster in 1871 destroyed some records — expect gaps
- **Note:** For a person who died testate (with a will), search will books; for intestate estates, search administration files

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state, not a rectangular-survey state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) holds original grants, warrants, surveys, and patents. Virginia granted lands in Kentucky before 1792. Per [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property): Old Kentucky Grants (1793-1856) and Kentucky Land Warrants (1816-1873) cover most of the target period
- **Types:** Deeds (person-to-person transfers), land grants and patents, warrants, surveys; deeds may name a wife by given name, a prior residence, or names of heirs
- **Date range:** County deed books from 1799; land grants from 1793 at the state level
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse holds deed books. Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) holds grants and patents. FamilySearch has *Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records, 1700-1955* — digitized images. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846-1848); Civil War (1861-1865) — the most significant; men on both Union and Confederate sides
- **Record types:** Service records and pension files at NARA; bounty land warrants (pre-1856); state adjutant general records at KDLA
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington DC and regional facilities) for federal records. KDLA (Frankfort) for state-level Kentucky military records. Fold3 (fold3.com, subscription) indexes many Civil War service and pension records

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Numerous rural family cemeteries and church cemeteries throughout Pulaski County; specific names were not listed in returned tool results
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (findagrave.com) covers many Kentucky cemeteries; BillionGraves is an additional resource
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual congregations and the Pulaski County Historical Society

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Specific paper names and dates for Pulaski County were not returned by the survey tools; Somerset was the county seat and likely had a local paper by the 1850s-1860s
- **Where held:** Newspapers.com (subscription) and the Kentucky Digital Library (kdl.kyvl.org) index Kentucky newspapers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate notices, and legal advertisements supplement sparse vital records

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Pulaski County is inland; any immigrant ancestors likely arrived through East Coast ports (Baltimore, New York, Philadelphia, New Orleans). The Cumberland Gap corridor brought many early settlers overland
- **Record types:** Passenger lists at NARA; naturalization records at the Pulaski County Circuit Court (pre-1906, naturalizations could be filed in any court of record); alien registrations (post-period)
- **Where held:** NARA for passenger lists. Pulaski County Courthouse for local naturalizations. FamilySearch and Ancestry index pre-1906 naturalizations
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members

### Tax records
- **Types:** County property tax lists and personal property tax lists
- **Date range:** From county formation (1799)
- **Where held:** KDLA holds microfilmed Kentucky county tax lists. Some are on FamilySearch and Ancestry
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are available for every year (not just census years) and can document a person's presence in the county between censuses or substitute for missing census years

### Other record types
- **County court minute books:** Record county business beyond litigation — road assignments, poor relief, payments to local officials, and other matters naming residents
- **Pulaski County Historical Society vertical files:** The society maintains surname files and the most comprehensive local church record and obituary collection per the FamilySearch Wiki
- **Town and county histories:** 19th- and early 20th-century county histories often transcribe early records and may be the only surviving copy of records since lost

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Will books 1801-1929 (digitized); marriage bonds 1799-1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818-1995; Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839-1960; Kentucky Marriages 1785-1979; Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843-1970; Kentucky Land Office records 1700-1955 | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | Federal census, county tax lists, vital records indexes, land grants | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Civil War service records, pension files | Subscription |
| Find A Grave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal census images, military records, passenger lists | Free/fee |

**Coverage of this survey:** The `collections_search` tool returned 0 results at both the county and Kentucky state level; `volume_search` similarly returned 0 results at both levels; `catalog_search` returned 0 hits at both levels. All three tools returned an empty resolved place (`standardPlace: ""`), indicating a place-resolution gap in the tools during this session — not confirmed absence of records. The FamilySearch Wiki for Pulaski County specifically names digitized collections available on FamilySearch. Researchers should search FamilySearch and Ancestry directly rather than relying on these tool-returned counts.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, 100 N. Main St. #208, Somerset, KY 42502 | Marriage bonds and licenses from 1799; deed books from 1799; court order books from 1799; wills and probate from 1801 | In-person or mail request |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records; state military records | In-person; some records online via kdla.ky.gov |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscripts, newspapers, genealogical collections, land records | In-person; some digital resources |
| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset | Surname vertical files; church records; local newspaper obituaries | In-person; contact society for hours |
| University of Kentucky Special Collections, Lexington | Manuscripts, county histories, regional collections | In-person |

## Records NOT online
- Full county deed books (beyond the land grant/patent collections) — courthouse or KDLA microfilm
- Court order books and civil/criminal case files — courthouse or KDLA microfilm
- Pre-1911 county birth and death registers from the partial registration periods (1853-1862 and 1874-1878) — KDLA microfilm; compliance was poor and many registers are incomplete
- Local church registers not captured in FamilySearch's incomplete Kentucky Church Records collection — individual congregations or Pulaski County Historical Society
- County tax lists for most years — KDLA microfilm (some on FamilySearch and Ancestry)
- Sexton and burial records from private cemeteries

## Known record losses
The [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki page](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) states that a disaster destroyed some county records in 1838 and again in 1871. The 1871 loss falls within the target period and may affect court, deed, and probate records created before that date. No tool result specified which record series were lost or survived. Researchers should contact the Pulaski County Courthouse and KDLA to determine which specific volumes survived.

## Research tips
- Vital events in 1840-1880 are largely undocumented in civil records due to poor compliance with county registration laws (active only 1853-1862 and 1874-1878 per [Kentucky Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)). Prioritize church registers, mortality schedules, and cemetery records for births and deaths
- Marriage bonds are the most complete vital-event record series for the period — they are county-level from 1799 and are digitized on FamilySearch through 1871 per [Pulaski County, Kentucky Genealogy wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- Kentucky land records are state-land (not federal-land): look to the Kentucky Land Office in Frankfort for grants and patents, not the BLM General Land Office. Deed books at the county courthouse record person-to-person transfers and often name wives by given name, prior residences, and heirs. Source: [Kentucky Land and Property](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- The Pulaski County Historical Society maintains surname vertical files and holds the most comprehensive local church record and obituary collection — contact them early in research
- Tax lists exist for every year and can document presence in the county when census records are missing or when a person is between federal enumerations
- Civil War service affected virtually every family; Kentucky men served on both Union and Confederate sides. Search both sets of records at NARA and on Fold3
- The 1871 records disaster means some courthouse records from before that date are lost — when a deed or court record is missing, check whether a contemporary copy or abstract survives in the KDLA microfilm or in county history publications
- Neighboring counties were not listed in the returned tool results (the Pulaski County Genealogy page did not include a Neighboring Counties table). Identify and check all bordering counties — families near county lines frequently generated records on both sides

output.text_response:
Researching an ancestor in the Alabama region around 1800 means working in the **Mississippi Territory**, not the state of Alabama, which did not exist until 1819. Here is an overview of the key archives and record repositories for that locality and period:

---

## Alabama Region (Mississippi Territory) circa 1800 — Locality Research Guide

### Jurisdictional Context
Alabama was part of the **Mississippi Territory** from 1798 until Alabama's own territorial organization in 1817, and statehood came in 1819. The earliest Alabama counties (Madison, Washington, Baldwin) were not established until around 1809, so most pre-county records fall under territorial or colonial-era governance.

---

### Primary Repositories

#### Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH) — Montgomery, AL
The single most important repository for this period:
- **Territorial census schedules**: 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810
- **Militia rolls**
- **Tax lists**

#### County Probate Courts
County-level records begin around **1809** (when the first Alabama counties were established). These hold deeds, wills, estates, and marriage bonds.

#### National Archives (NARA)
- **Federal land patents and land entry files** (General Land Office records)
- **Military files** (War of 1812, militia records)

---

### Colonial-Era Repositories (Mobile Area)
If your ancestor was near the Mobile district, prior colonial powers left records that must also be consulted:

- **Spanish-era land grants and registers**: Archivo General de Indias (Seville, Spain) — copies at the Library of Congress
- **French colonial records**: Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer (Aix-en-Provence, France)

---

### FamilySearch Collections
FamilySearch has both **indexed** and **browse-only** Alabama/territorial collections:

| Collection | Coverage | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Church records | From 1803 | Indexed |
| County marriages | From 1809 | Indexed |
| Probate records | From 1809 | Indexed |
| Census substitutes | 1810 | Indexed |
| Territorial court, land & deed records | Pre-statehood | Browse-only (image by image) |

---

### Important Caveats
- **No civil birth or death registration** existed in this period — vital events must be reconstructed from church registers, probate, and family bibles.

## Jurisdiction overview

- **County seat / administrative center:** Natchez (Mississippi Territory capital); St. Stephens (Alabama Territory capital)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Mississippi Territory (1798–1817), then Alabama Territory (1817–1819)
- **Population during period:** No population figures were returned by the tools for this period. The region was sparsely settled before the Creek War of 1813–1814; significant American migration followed.
- **Economy:** Subsistence agriculture and early cotton cultivation; fur trade in the interior; maritime trade at Mobile
- **Ethnic composition:** Creek and Cherokee nations in the interior; American settlers arriving from the Carolinas, Virginia, and Georgia; French and Spanish Creole communities around Mobile
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist and Methodist frontier congregations among American settlers; Catholic parishes in Mobile (colonial legacy); Presbyterian circuits in the Tennessee Valley region
- **Key historical events:** Creek War of 1813–1814 opened central Alabama to American settlement; U.S. seizure of Mobile from Spain in 1813 unified the region under American authority

## Boundary changes
- Before 1798, the Mobile area was under Spanish authority (1780–1813); interior Alabama was largely Creek and Cherokee territory under nominal Spanish or British claims.
- Mississippi Territory (est. 1798) initially covered the southern strip of present-day Alabama and Mississippi. It was enlarged in 1804 and again in 1813 to include the Mobile district after U.S. seizure.
- Alabama Territory separated from Mississippi Territory on 3 March 1817.
- Alabama became a state 14 December 1819.
- **Key quirk:** Records created 1798–1817 are filed under the Mississippi Territory. The territorial record series continues without a break into early Alabama statehood; treat them as one continuous research trail, not two separate jurisdictions.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** No civil registration of births, marriages, or deaths existed in the territorial period. The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Alabama Vital Records returned only generic content and do not state a statewide registration start year. - **What exists:** County-level marriage bonds and registers from county formation dates. No indexed civil birth or death records exist for the ca. 1800 period.
- **Where held:** Alabama county probate courts (originals); FamilySearch collection 'Alabama, County Marriages, 1809–1950' (id: 1598408, 612,345 records, 1,224,690 persons, 306,172 images — indexed + images): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1598408
- **Gaps:** No vital registration for births or deaths in the territorial period.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptismal, marriage, and burial registers; territorial census schedules; county probate records.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Catholic (Mobile colonial legacy), Baptist, Methodist, Presbyterian frontier congregations
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations. Catholic registers from the Mobile area predate 1800 and are among the oldest records for the region.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch collection 'Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950' (id: 1986396, 156,789 records, 78,394 images — indexed + images): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1986396. Spanish colonial Catholic registers for the Mobile area are held at the Archivo General de Indias (Seville), with copies at the Library of Congress, per the FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Genealogy page: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records. French colonial church records are at the Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer (Aix-en-Provence) and the Mobile Municipal Archives.
- **Language:** Spanish and French for Mobile-area colonial registers (pre-1813).

### Census records
- **Territorial censuses:** Enumerations were conducted in 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 within the Mississippi Territory covering present-day Alabama. These are held at the Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH) in Montgomery, per the FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Genealogy page: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records.
- **Federal census:** The 1810 federal census is the first to fully cover present-day Alabama and is available via FamilySearch. The 1800 federal census coverage for this region is incomplete.
- **Other enumerations:** Spanish colonial census returns for the Mobile district (pre-1813) are at the Archivo General de Indias.
- **Access:** FamilySearch 'Alabama, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1810–1890' (id: 2016756, 287,634 records — name-indexed, no images): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2016756. FamilySearch 'Mississippi, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes, 1792–1890' (id: 1927171, 198,340 records) may also include territorial-era Alabama enumerations: https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1927171.

- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories, petitions; territorial court records
- **Date range:** County-level probate from county formation dates (earliest FamilySearch coverage: 1809)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch 'Alabama, Probate Records, 1809–1985' (id: 1537764, 438,210 records, 219,105 images — indexed + images): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1537764. Both are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image. Territorial court records also held at ADAH.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Federal rectangular survey (township and range) — Alabama is a federal land state.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The U.S. General Land Office (GLO) issued federal land patents from the territorial period. Pre-American grants were issued by Spanish and British colonial authorities.
- **Types:** Federal patents, Spanish land grants, territorial court land records, county deeds, tax lists

- **Where held:** BLM GLO website (https://glorecords.blm.gov/) for federal patents. FamilySearch browse-only volume 004512889 (214 images, 1808–1819, territorial court and land records). ADAH holds colonial Spanish land grant records for the Mobile area.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Creek War 1813–1814; War of 1812; territorial militia service

- **Major cemeteries:** Family and church burial grounds predominated; formal cemeteries were rare before statehood.

- **Physical records:** Few formal sexton records exist for the territorial period.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Territorial-period newspaper presence in present-day Alabama was extremely limited; the Mobile area had the earliest papers.

| Archivo General de Indias, Seville | Spanish colonial records: Mobile district census, church registers, land grants | In-person or via PARES digital portal |
| Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence | French colonial records of the Mobile area | In-person |
| Library of Congress, Washington DC | Copies of Spanish and French colonial records | In-person / online catalog |
| Mobile Municipal Archives | Copies of colonial records; early Mobile city records | In-person |
| National Archives (NARA), Atlanta region | Federal territorial records, military files, pension records | In-person / online databases |

## Records NOT online
- Territorial census schedules (1801, 1805, 1808, 1810) for present-day Alabama are at ADAH and are not available on FamilySearch or Ancestry.
- Spanish colonial census returns and notarial records for the Mobile district are physically at the Archivo General de Indias; some are digitized via PARES but are not in major U.S. genealogical databases.
- French colonial records of the Mobile area are at the Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer and Mobile Municipal Archives; not in major U.S. online databases.
- Most county tax lists and territorial court minute books for ca. 1800 are in physical form at ADAH or county courthouses.
- Territorial militia rolls are at ADAH and are not fully indexed online.

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey identified specific losses of Alabama territorial records. The surviving FamilySearch browse-only volumes and the wiki_search results indicate partial survival of territorial court, land, and county deed records, though coverage is fragmentary. Absence of an online collection does not indicate record loss — many county-level series were never digitized.

## Research tips
- Search under 'Mississippi Territory' and the Mississippi state-level collections as well as 'Alabama' for any record dated before December 1819. The same continuous series of land, court, and tax records spans both sides of the statehood date. Per the FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Genealogy page: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records
- If your ancestor was in the Mobile area before 1813, the Spanish colonial records are the primary source. These are distributed across the Archivo General de Indias (Seville), Library of Congress, and Mobile Municipal Archives. Per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records
- The territorial census schedules of 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 are the best substitute for the federal census in this period and should be consulted at ADAH before assuming no census coverage exists.
- Two FamilySearch digitized volumes for the Alabama area (1803–1820) must be browsed image by image; there is no name search for these volumes.
- Alabama is a federal land state (rectangular survey); search the BLM GLO website (https://glorecords.blm.gov/) for territorial-era federal land patents before searching county deed books for the original grant.
- Church records — especially Catholic registers in the Mobile area — are the primary source for births, marriages, and deaths before county record formation. No civil vital registration existed in the territorial period.
- Note: All four FamilySearch Wiki place pages for Alabama returned only generic content during this survey. Consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy directly for the wiki's full research strategy for this state.

output.text_response:
Locality guide saved as **loc_001** in the project.

---

Researching ancestors in the Arkansas region before 1800 means working in a territory that had no independent existence yet — it was the far northwestern edge of **Spanish Louisiana**, centered almost entirely on a single garrison settlement called **Arkansas Post**. Records from that world are colonial documents held mostly in Little Rock and Seville, Spain, written in French or Spanish.

**Key facts about the records:**

- Only one small collection — **64 pages of Catholic sacramental registers (1763–1800)** — has been digitized on FamilySearch. It has no name index and must be read page by page in Spanish (FamilySearch image group **008814402**).

**Essential repositories:**

| Repository | What They Hold |
|---|---|
| **Arkansas History Commission** (Little Rock) | U.S.-based colonial holdings; contact for a finding aid |
| **Roman Catholic Diocese of Little Rock** | Original Catholic church registers for Arkansas Post |
| **Archivo General de Indias** (Seville, Spain) | Military, land, and administrative records that never left Spain |

**Recommended next steps:**

1. Contact the **Arkansas History Commission** for a finding aid to their colonial holdings.
2. Browse or order FamilySearch image group **008814402** (the digitized Catholic registers, 1763–1800) — no index, page-by-page reading required.
3. Assess whether the research trail continues into the Spanish archives in Seville (Archivo General de Indias), especially for military service, land grants, or administrative correspondence.

Given how sparse the surviving record base is, **the Catholic sacramental registers and the Spanish colonial archives in Seville** represent the two best hopes for pre-1800 Arkansas ancestry.
